title: Evil Geniuses: Delving into the Safety of LLM-based Agents
scope_rationale: Some claims concern interaction-amplified jailbreak risk, but the paper predates a precise independently-stateful-agent boundary and several results are general role-prompt jailbreak findings.

title: Cooperation, Competition, and Maliciousness: LLM-Stakeholders Interactive Negotiation
scope_rationale: Maliciousness and information sharing are measured in multi-party negotiation.

title: PsySafe: A Comprehensive Framework for Psychological-based Attack Defense and Evaluation of Multi-agent System Safety
scope_rationale: Interaction and collective danger are central, but the paper primarily studies broad psychological safety and role-prompt effects rather than a narrowly defined technical security property.

title: A Survey on Trustworthy LLM Agents: Threats and Countermeasures
scope_rationale: The survey covers MAS, but it is not interaction-primary and includes broad trustworthiness dimensions.

title: AgentBreeder: Mitigating the AI Safety Risks of Multi-Agent Scaffolds via Self-Improvement
scope_rationale: The work evaluates safety properties of composed agent scaffolds and searches for unsafe configurations, but its primary evidence is benchmark safety under architecture search rather than a technical runtime security threat model.

title: AI Agents Under Threat: A Survey of Key Security Challenges and Future Pathways
scope_rationale: Primary boundary is general AI agents and four knowledge gaps, not LLM-MAS interaction as the sole object.

title: Alignment Tipping Process: How Self-Evolution Pushes LLM Agents Off the Rails
scope_rationale: The MAS diffusion pathway informs collective objective integrity, but there is no explicit adversary and half the paper is single-agent self-evolution.
attack_instance_coding_required: no as attack; yes in failure/evaluation ledger

title: Breaking Agents: Compromising Autonomous LLM Agents Through Malfunction Amplification
scope_rationale: The attack primitive is general agent malfunction. Only the advanced viral cases are interaction-dependent and should enter the MAS claim corpus.

title: Chasing Moving Targets with Online Self-Play Reinforcement Learning for Safer Language Models
scope_rationale: Retained after the citation retrieval gate and security scope screen.

title: Decentralized Multi-Agent System with Trust-Aware Communication
scope_rationale: Trust scores govern communication among decentralized agents.

title: Formalizing the Safety Security and Functional Properties of Agentic AI Systems
scope_rationale: It formalizes cross-protocol safety/security properties but is broader than LLM-MAS security and includes agent-tool composition.

title: Goal-Aware Identification and Rectification of Misinformation in Multi-Agent Systems
scope_rationale: It evaluates intentional misinformation injection and downstream multi-agent task integrity, but much of the endpoint is task performance/toxicity rather than a formal CIA/authorization property.

title: Here Comes the AI Worm: Preventing the Propagation of Adversarial Self-Replicating Prompts Within GenAI Ecosystems
scope_rationale: The work studies a network of GenAI email and RAG applications and users. It is highly relevant to propagation, but the system boundary is broader than a population of independently stateful LLM agent cores.

title: IBGP: Imperfect Byzantine Generals Problem for Zero-Shot Robustness in Communicative Multi-Agent Systems
scope_rationale: The paper studies adversarial coordination robustness, but its task environments and redefined partial-coordination property are broader reliability/safety and should not be treated as classical security consensus.

title: NetSafe: Exploring the Topological Safety of Multi-agent System
scope_rationale: The paper mixes adversarial misinformation or harmful content with broader hallucination, bias, fairness, and reliability phenomena. Only the adversarial security claims should enter core-security statistics.

title: On the Resilience of LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration with Faulty Agents
scope_rationale: The study covers malicious as well as clumsy/faulty agents and is fundamentally a resilience/reliability evaluation rather than a purely adversarial attack paper.

title: Reproducibility Study of Cooperation, Competition, and Maliciousness: LLM-Stakeholders Interactive Negotiation
scope_rationale: The study reproduces maliciousness, information leakage, and fairness effects in interacting LLM stakeholders.

title: Revisiting Multi-Agent Debate as Test-Time Scaling: A Systematic Study of Conditional Effectiveness
scope_rationale: Retained after the citation retrieval gate and security scope screen.

title: Stop Reducing Responsibility in LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Systems to Local Alignment
scope_rationale: The position paper includes adversarial vulnerability and global oversight but is primarily responsible-AI/governance theory.

title: Teaching Models to Balance Resisting and Accepting Persuasion
scope_rationale: Adversarial persuasion and resistance are evaluated in recursive dialogues and multi-agent debate.

title: The Dark Side of LLMs: Agent-based Attack Vectors for System-level Compromise
scope_rationale: The inter-agent provenance/authorization claim is core, but the paper as a whole is a broader agent system-compromise comparison and not exclusively MAS.

title: The Emerged Security and Privacy of LLM Agent: A Survey with Case Studies
scope_rationale: Primary object is general LLM agents across planning, memory, tools, interaction, and deployment.

title: To Trust or Not to Trust: Attention-based Trust Management for LLM Multi-Agent Systems
scope_rationale: It addresses malicious/unreliable message influence, but the taxonomy mixes deception, toxicity, irrelevance, low quality, and reliability; claim-level security coding is required.

title: Understanding the Information Propagation Effects of Communication Topologies in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
scope_rationale: The measured effect is information propagation under different communication graphs.

title: A Trace-Based Assurance Framework for Agentic AI Orchestration: Contracts, Testing, and Governance
scope_rationale: Assurance contracts and traces cover orchestrated agent workflows.

title: Agent Drift: Quantifying Behavioral Degradation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems Over Extended Interactions
scope_rationale: Retained after the citation retrieval gate and security scope screen.

title: AI Agents with Decentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials
scope_rationale: DIDs and verifiable credentials bind identities in agent-to-agent interactions.

title: Among Us: Measuring and Mitigating Malicious Contributions in Model Collaboration Systems
scope_rationale: The malicious-contributor problem is important, but only a subset of the four collaboration levels cleanly satisfies the SoK’s strict LLM-MAS interaction boundary.

title: ATAG: AI-Agent Application Threat Assessment with Attack Graphs
scope_rationale: Attack graphs model compromise paths across agentic application components and interactions.

title: Beyond Goodhart's Law: A Dynamic Benchmark for Evaluating Compliance in Multi-Agent Systems
scope_rationale: Procedural compliance, authorization, privacy, and trace integrity are security-relevant, but the work is not exclusively MAS and many violations are governance/compliance rather than adversarial security.

title: CalBench: Evaluating Coordination-Privacy Trade-offs in Multi-Agent LLMs
scope_rationale: The benchmark primarily studies coordination, cost, fairness, and communication; privacy leakage is one first-class metric but no adversary is required.

title: Deception and Communication in Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems: An Experimental Study with Among Us
scope_rationale: It is a social-deception evaluation in a game with assigned adversarial roles, not a general technical attack or defense study.
attack_instance_coding_required: no for attack taxonomy; yes for deception/communication evidence

title: Deliberation and drift: Evaluating alignment fragility in multi-agent medical artificial intelligence
scope_rationale: Alignment fragility is evaluated as an effect of multi-agent deliberation.

title: From Shield to Target: Denial-of-Service Attacks on LLM-Based Agent Guardrails
scope_rationale: Shared-monitor resource isolation is interaction-amplified, but the underlying guardrail DoS is not MAS-native and MAS is only one of several deployment evaluations.

title: From Tasks to Teams: A Risk-First Evaluation Framework for Multi-Agent LLM Systems in Finance
scope_rationale: The evaluation targets risks that emerge at team and workflow level in a financial MAS.

title: LieCraft: A Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Deceptive Capabilities in Language Models
scope_rationale: It measures deception capability and peer detection in controlled games, but the malicious objective is assigned by the benchmark rather than arising from a deployment attack.
attack_instance_coding_required: no standalone attack instance; code deception conditions and outcomes

title: Parasites in the Toolchain: A Large-Scale Analysis of Attacks on the MCP Ecosystem
venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy
scope_rationale: The system is one LLM host composing multiple MCP servers and tools. It is directly relevant to distributed capability composition but does not necessarily contain multiple independently stateful LLM agent cores.

title: Resilience in Ambient Multi-Agent LLMs via Decentralized Bio-Autonomic Control and Immune-Inspired Anomaly Detection
scope_rationale: The paper mixes fault resilience, anomaly detection, privacy-preserving adaptation, and malicious-agent/control-flow scenarios. The interaction is genuine, but not every evaluated perturbation is adversarial security.

title: ResMAS: Resilience Optimization in LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
scope_rationale: Primary perturbations are random agent failures and general resilience, not consistently malicious adversaries. It is important design-time robustness evidence but should not be treated as a pure attack-defense paper.
attack_instance_coding_required: no for attack corpus; yes for defense/design coverage

title: RiskLab: A Controlled Toolkit for Probing Emergent Risks in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
scope_rationale: It probes collusion, resource overreach, drift, and strategic misreporting, but includes broad emergent risk and reliability concerns beyond adversarial security.
attack_instance_coding_required: yes only at individual probe/claim level

title: Security Threat Modeling for Emerging AI-Agent Protocols: A Comparative Analysis of MCP A2A Agora and ANP
scope_rationale: Protocol security is directly relevant, but the four-protocol corpus is not exclusively multiagent and includes a tool protocol.

title: Semantic Intent Fragmentation: A Single-Shot Compositional Attack on Multi-Agent AI Pipelines
scope_rationale: Strongly relevant to global-vs-local observability and composition, but may be an agentic pipeline rather than a strict LLM-MAS under the proposed boundary.

title: Social Dynamics as Critical Vulnerabilities that Undermine Objective Decision-Making in LLM Collectives
scope_rationale: Intentional adversarial peers manipulate objective decisions, but the study is also a social-psychology evaluation and does not model a broader technical security boundary.

title: SoK: Attack and Defense Landscape of Agentic AI Systems
scope_rationale: The paper is core agentic-AI security but not MAS-primary; it is the key single-agent/component-centric comparator.

title: The Subtle Art of Defection: Understanding Uncooperative Behaviors in LLM based Multi-Agent Systems
scope_rationale: Defection is defined through strategic behavior among interacting agents.

title: The Trust Paradox in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems: When Collaboration Becomes a Security Vulnerability
venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Social Systems
scope_rationale: The paper mixes ordinary over-sharing and malicious requests; confidentiality/authorization claims are security-relevant, but not every trust-utility result is an attack claim.

title: Thought Virus: Viral Misalignment via Subliminal Prompting in Multi-Agent Systems
scope_rationale: Interaction-dependent covert propagation and monitorability are relevant, but the primary outcomes are controlled concept preferences/truthfulness rather than a conventional adversarial system compromise.

title: TRiSM for Agentic AI: A Review of Trust Risk and Security Management in LLM-based Agentic Multi-Agent Systems
scope_rationale: Security is one TRiSM pillar among explainability, ModelOps, privacy, and lifecycle governance.

title: ValueFlow: Measuring the Propagation of Value Perturbations in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
scope_rationale: The work audits value propagation and collective susceptibility but uses controlled perturbations without a deployment adversary.
attack_instance_coding_required: no attack instance; code perturbation/evaluation conditions

title: Whispering Agents: An Event-Driven Covert Communication Protocol for the Internet of Agents
scope_rationale: It is a dual-use covert communication protocol for paired agents. It directly informs covert coordination and observer scope but is not inherently a malicious attack or evidence of spontaneous collusion.
